jen_acme: Hey support — after upgrading to redwood-sdk 1.4.0 and installing with poetry extras (poetry add redwood-sdk[full]) our service fails on startup with ImportError: 'cannot import name AsyncClient from httpx'. Happening in CI Docker image and on staging. Anyone seen this?

maria_support: @jen_acme can you paste the stack + poetry/pip output? Which python version and how are you installing in CI?

jen_acme: Python 3.10.7, poetry 1.5.1. CI Dockerfile uses python:3.10-slim. Stack trace: ```
File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood_sdk/http_client.py", line 12, in <module>
  from httpx import AsyncClient
ImportError: cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'httpx' (unknown location)
```
And pip freeze in a failing CI job shows: ```
httpx==0.24.1
redwood-sdk==1.4.0
typing-extensions==4.4.0
```

james_devx: AsyncClient definitely exists in httpx normally. Two things to check: 1) shadowed module named httpx in repo? 2) transitive dep forcing older typing-extensions/httpx variant.

jen_acme: no file named httpx in repo. Also seeing runtime warnings: "module 'typing_extensions' has no attribute 'TypeAlias'" — which makes me think typing-extensions too old.

oskar_eng: typing_extensions 4.4.0 is missing some newer symbols. It can be pulled in by other deps (pydantic, etc). Also poetry lockfile can resolve different httpx versions depending on constraints.

maria_support: Can you try reproducing in a clean venv and run these exact steps?
1) python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
2) python -m pip install --upgrade pip
3) pip install "redwood-sdk[full]==1.4.0"
4) python -c "import httpx; print(httpx.__version__); from redwood_sdk import Client"
Share results.

jen_acme: I ran that locally. It installed httpx 0.23.3 even though our lockfile said 0.24.1. CI install log shows: "Installing httpx (0.23.3) ..." so something in our lockfile or cache is odd.

maria_support: Poetry caching + installer differences can do that. Quick mitigation: pin constraints in pyproject.toml: `httpx = ">=0.23.0,<0.25"` and bump typing-extensions to `>=4.5.0`. If you can't change that quickly, try installing redwood-sdk 1.4.1 — we shipped a patch that guards the import and patches an idempotency/retry path.

james_devx: Note: there was a bug in 1.4.0 where, in some retry code paths, the `Idempotency-Key` header was not preserved which could lead to duplicate non-idempotent calls being retried. That was fixed in 1.4.1. If you saw duplicate billing records around the same timeframe as the import issues, the SDK bug could be related.

jen_acme: Installed 1.4.1 locally and the ImportError went away. CI still failed until I cleared caches — turns out our CI caches a venv/wheel cache with typing-extensions 4.4.0. Clearing the cache + installing 1.4.1 made CI green.

oskar_eng: Thanks for the repro steps. For the duplicate billing concern: can you capture the request logs (redwood request-id, headers) and paste them? We need to confirm whether `Idempotency-Key` was missing on retry. If so, we should escalate for potential billing remediation.

maria_support: Action items: 1) customer to upgrade to redwood-sdk 1.4.1 (short term fix) 2) pin httpx and typing-extensions in pyproject/constraints (recommended) 3) clear CI caches and rebuild lockfile if needed 4) customer to share request logs for suspected duplicate charges so we can correlate with server logs.

jen_acme: Repro steps I used in CI: Dockerfile snippet: ```
FROM python:3.10-slim
COPY pyproject.toml poetry.lock /app/
WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install poetry && poetry config virtualenvs.create false && poetry install --no-dev
COPY . /app
RUN pytest -q
```
I did `poetry lock --no-update` and still saw an older httpx in the installed set until I cleared the Docker layer cache.

maria_support: Good details — caching layers + poetry + pinned dependencies can cause those surprises. We'll open an engineering ticket to trace the idempotency header bug and check if any customers saw duplicate charges.

deploy-bot: Created ENG-2432: "python-sdk: import/retry/idempotency fixes (1.4.1)" assigned to oskar_eng, priority: high, customer: acme.

jen_acme: Thanks all — 1.4.1 + clearing CI cache fixed our pipeline and app. I'll send logs if I spot duplicate billing.

maria_support: Great — marking as resolved on our side until you confirm billing. Reopen if new evidence appears. :thumbsup:
